validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real via multiple genuinely independent origins spanning 2006-2018, none GEM-derived. (1) FERC/Federal Register: a continuous docket history at CP07-52 (Downeast LNG, Inc. terminal) and CP07-53 (Downeast Pipeline, LLC pipeline certificate) running from the original Dec 22, 2006 certificate application (FR notice E6-22691, Jan 8, 2007) through a 2009 draft EIS (E9-12076), a 2013 supplemental draft EIS (2013-07795), and a 2014 final EIS (2014-11861) -- all describing a real, actively-reviewed 29.8-mile/30-inch natural gas pipeline from a proposed Robbinston, ME LNG terminal to an interconnect with Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline near Baileyville, ME. (2) Pipeline News (Pipeline & Gas Journal trade publication), Oct-2018 'Planned Projects' PDF, independently extracted via pdfplumber after pdftotext -layout garbled its multi-column layout: a 'Downeast Pipeline' entry (Operator: Downeast Pipeline LLC; Length 30 mi; Diameter 30 in; Location Robbinston, ME; Capacity 300 MMcf/d; Status 'Project has currently been denied'). (3) DOE/FE Federal Register notice 2017-13233 (Orders During April 2017): Order 3600-A, dated 04/21/17, in FE Docket Nos. 14-172-LNG/14-173-LNG, granting Downeast LNG, Inc.'s own request to vacate its LNG export authority and withdraw its non-FTA export application -- a real company taking a real, dated regulatory action to wind the project down. (4) SEC EDGAR: Star Gas Partners LP's FY2011 10-K names 'Downeast LNG, Inc.' as a real non-public company in which director Paul Vermylen's investment vehicle, Kestrel Energy Partners LLC, held an equity interest -- an independent federal securities disclosure. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a natural-gas import/sendout pipeline (interstate natural gas transmission facility under NGA section 7(c)), captive to the Downeast LNG import terminal -- not gathering, not a different commodity. DUPLICATE: checked the current GGIT gas snapshot for every Maine-touching row and every 'Downeast'-named row -- only P0321 exists; the only other Maine gas pipeline in the tracker (P0242, Portland Natural Gas Transmission System / PNGTS, Pittsburg NH-Westbrook ME) is a wholly separate, pre-existing interstate system with no route or corporate overlap. Not a relabeling of any roster row.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's CancelledYear=2013 cannot be right: FERC's OWN final EIS notice (2014-11861, published May 22, 2014) confirms the Downeast LNG/Downeast Pipeline project was still under active federal environmental review a full year AFTER the recorded cancellation year, following a supplemental draft EIS in April 2013 (2013-07795) that was itself part of ongoing, not terminated, review. No dated cancellation/withdrawal/denial document from 2013 was found anywhere (FERC, DOE, SEC, trade press, open web). The clearest DATED formal termination event found is DOE/FE Order 3600-A (April 21, 2017; FR notice 2017-13233), in which Downeast LNG, Inc. itself requested to vacate its long-term LNG export authority and withdraw its non-FTA export application -- a sponsor-initiated, dated federal regulatory wind-down. Pipeline News's Oct-2018 entry ('Project has currently been denied') independently confirms the project was dead by late 2018, consistent with (not contradicting) the 2017 DOE action. Scope note: the DOE order is captioned 'Downeast LNG, Inc.' (the terminal entity) and FERC never published a distinct Federal Register notice terminating Downeast Pipeline, LLC's own CP07-53 certificate docket specifically -- no FERC filing after the May-2014 final EIS was found in Federal Register full-text search on 'Downeast Pipeline'. But this pipeline is a single-purpose captive sendout line with no function apart from the LNG terminal (per every FERC filing, it exists solely to move regasified LNG from this one terminal to the interstate grid), so the terminal sponsor's formal, dated wind-down is treated as dispositive of the pipeline's fate too -- the same kind of sibling-entity/parent-record inference already used elsewhere in this batch (e.g., P0322's SEC-subsidiary-list dating). Held at medium tier for that reason, not high.

The sheet's Location unit is flagged irregular because StartLocation and EndLocation are BOTH recorded as 'Robbinston' -- i.e. a zero-length placeholder, not a real route. FERC's 2009 draft EIS notice (E9-12076) states explicitly: 'Downeast's proposed 29.8-mile-long pipeline would transport natural gas from the LNG terminal to an interconnect point with Maritimes and Northeast Pipeline's L.L.C. (M&NE) existing pipeline system near the town of Baileyville, Maine.' Robbinston (the LNG terminal site, 748 U.S. Route 1) is correctly the START; the pipeline's actual END is the M&NE interconnect near Baileyville, ME -- both towns in Washington County, Maine, consistent with every FERC filing's 'Washington County, Maine' project-area description. This is the only FERC document found that names the specific end-town (later notices describe the pipeline only by length/diameter without repeating the town name), so this is single-origin (FERC) evidence; Pipeline News's PDF entry gives only a single 'Location: Robbinston, ME' field with no start/end split, so it neither confirms nor contradicts. Held at medium tier accordingly, but the finding is unambiguous: recording the same town for both ends of a 29.8-mile pipeline is definitely wrong regardless of which specific end-town is used.
